Subject: Follow-up: token volumes & target $/1M benchmarks (thanks for the call)

Hi Wei —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery:
- Primary use case: conversational assistant + routing + occasional embeddings for search.
- Expected phased rollout: pilot (Q2) ~50M tokens/month, scale to production (Q3-Q4) 300M-500M tokens/month, long-term peak could reach ~1B tokens/month depending on feature adoption.
- Traffic shape: spiky evenings (US), median seq length ~350 tokens for chat, embeddings ~500 tokens per request on average.
- Key procurement targets: 1) predictable unit economics, 2) ability to pin model versions, 3) compliance (SOC2) and audit logs.

You mentioned a target unit cost for budgeting. Could you confirm the target $/1M tokens you expect for the production phase (and separately for pilot)? From our quick benchmarking notes, customers commonly target a blended range of $10- $30 per 1M tokens for open-model hosting; incumbents (hosted/high-cap models) can run higher depending on model class. For planning, it helps to know whether ACME is modeling to the low end (~$10/1M) or mid/high end (~$25- $50/1M).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm target $/1M for pilot and for production scaling
- We'll send a pricing benchmark sheet (attached) comparing Redwood list/discounted tiers vs approximate public host ranges (OpenAI/Anthropic/other hosts) and show unit economics at 50M, 300M, 1B/month volumes.
- If numbers align, we'll book a 30-min procurement sync next week to walk the commercial terms and preferred billing cadence.

I attached a quick pricing comparison and the token usage export you shared during the call (saved as acme-token-usage.csv).

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the numbers from our side:
- Pilot target: ~50M tokens/month (expected duration: 6-8 weeks)
- Production target (initial committed): 300M tokens/month, with ability to burst to ~500M/month during peak marketing campaigns
- Long-term planning: we want to budget for up to 1B tokens/month as a scenario but would not commit immediately.

Budgeting guidance from finance: our target blended price to model financials is $15/1M tokens for embeddings and non-real-time workloads, and $25/1M tokens for chat/generation in the short term. 2) Confirmation of baseline SLAs and whether dedicated capacity (reserved pools) has a materially different unit price vs hosted.

Vanessa / Marissa —

Thanks for including me. Quick internal note / suggested approach for the procurement call:

1) Offer structure (tiered):
   - Pilot (month-to-month / 50M): $40/1M tokens list, discount to $20/1M with a 2-month commitment; includes standard hosted SLA and access to Redwood Console.
   - Production commit (300M/month): starting at $18/1M tokens for hosted with a 12-month commit; option to move to Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) at $25/1M with a guaranteed latency SLO and prioritized capacity.
   - Scale (>=1B/month): custom pricing in the $10-3$15/1M range depending on model pinning, KV cache agreements, and a multi-year commit.

2) Benchmarks vs competitors: we should avoid quoting public list prices verbatim in the deck; instead show a competitive band:
   - OpenAI/Anthropic (hosted/high-cap models): typically higher for top-tier models, especially for large context/chat models - present as a comparative band in the deck.
   - Other open-model hosts: wide variance; emphasize Redwood's cost controls (batching, caching, quantization profiles) to drive lower effective $/1M at scale.

3) Ask procurement for their preferred billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and whether they need committed spend on a PO to get lower tiered pricing.

I drafted a quick pricing slide and marked the areas where we can be flexible (e.g., trial discount, faster onboarding credit, first-release SLA add-on).
